Rashi on Pesachim 43a:13:1.english: And for its mixture, [he violates] a prohibition - [This is derived] from [the verse] "anything leavened," as [explained] below.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:14:1.hebrew: מ"ט לא אמר כדרב יהודה - דמוקי מתניתין כר"מ: רב נחמן ס"ל, נוקשה בעיניה חמור מחמץ גמור ע"י תערובת:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:14:1.english: What is the reason he did not say like Rav Yehuda - who establishes our Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Meir: Rav Nachman holds [that] noksheh [imperfect leaven] in its pure state is more severe than full-fledged chametz [present] through a mixture.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:15:1.hebrew: רב נחמן <abbr title="סבירא ליה">ס"ל</abbr>, נוקשה בעיניה חמור מחמץ גמור <abbr title="על ידי">ע"י</abbr> תערובת:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:15:1.english: Rav Nachman holds [that] hardened [leaven] in its pure form is more severe than full-fledged leaven in a mixture.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:18:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרב יהודה - דאמר חמץ גמור בתערובת חמור. לענין כרת, לא כתיב כל מחמצת, אלא כל אוכל חמץ, ולקמן מפרש ליה. כותח ושכר וחומץ וזיתום — כולן חמץ גמור מעורב בהן: כותח איכא פת, ובהנך תלתא איכא שערי, וכולהו בני אכילה ושתיה נינהו. אבל זומן ועמילן וקולן, דנוקשה הוא ובעיניה, הואיל ולאו בני אכילה נינהו לא תנינהו. והיינו כדרב יהודה, דאמר: מודה היה ר"א בנוקשה בעיניה דפטור:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:18:1.english: It was taught [in a baraita] in accordance with Rav Yehuda - Who said [that] full-fledged chametz in a mixture is more stringent [than hardened chametz in its pure form]. Regarding karet, "any leavened thing" is not written, but rather "whoever eats leavened bread" (chametz), and later [the Gemara] explains it. Kutaḥ, beer, vinegar, and zitom — all of them have full-fledged chametz mixed into them: [in] kutaḥ there is bread, and in those [other] three there is barley, and all of them are fit for eating or drinking. However, broth (zoman), starch (amilan), and paste (kolan), which are hardened [chametz] and in their pure form, since they are not fit for eating, [the baraita] did not teach them. And this is in accordance with Rav Yehuda, who said [that] Rabbi Eliezer conceded regarding hardened [chametz] in its pure form that one is exempt.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:1:1.hebrew: שהגיעו לפרקן ולא הגיעו לשנים - שיש להן שערות כאילו הגיעו לפרקן, והן לא הגיעו לכלל שנים, ובושות על כך:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:1:1.english: [Girls] who reached their maturity, but had not reached [the requisite] years - [Meaning] that they have hair as though they had reached their maturity, yet they have not reached the [full] years [of majority], and they are embarrassed about this.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:1:2.english: Wealthy [women], they smear them with fine flour - And [it] causes the hair to fall out.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:20:1.hebrew: ור"א עירובו בלאו מנא ליה - פשיטא, מדאפקיה בלשון מחמצת, וגבי כרת נמי מחמצת כתיב:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:20:1.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, from where does he [derive] its mixture in a prohibition? - [It is] obvious, since [Scripture] expressed it with the term machmetzet ["anything leavened"], and regarding karet [excision] as well, machmetzet is written.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:22:1.hebrew: ההוא - מחמצת דגבי כרת לאו לעירובו אתא, אלא לנתחמץ מחמת דבר אחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:22:1.english: That - [meaning, the word] "leavened" [written] in connection with karet, does not come for its mixture, rather for [an item] that became leavened due to a different factor.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:23:1.hebrew: אי הכי - האי דגבי לאו נמי אימא לאזהורי אנתחמץ מחמת דבר אחר אתא, ואזהרה דתערובת מנא ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:23:1.english: If so - This [phrase] regarding the prohibition as well, say [that] it comes to warn against [food] that became leavened through something else, and from where [does one derive] the prohibition of a mixture?

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:25:1.hebrew: התם נמי - גבי כרת, הא כתיב "כל אוכל מחמצת ונכרתה":
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:25:1.english: There, too - Regarding karet, is it not written: "Whosoever eats anything leavened, [that soul] shall be cut off"?

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:26:1.hebrew: לכל עונשין - מכאן שהנשים חייבות על כל לא תעשה שבתורה, שהרי עונשן מלקות:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:26:1.english: For all punishments - From here [we derive] that women are liable for every negative commandment in the Torah, since their punishment is lashes.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:2:1.english: Setaket - It has not been explained.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:3:1.hebrew: אנפיקינון - במנחות תנן: אנפקינון לא יביא, ומפרש ר' יהודה: אנפקינין הוא שמן זית כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:3:1.english: Anpikinon - In Menachot we learned [in a Mishnah]: "One may not bring anpikinon," and Rabbi Yehuda explains: anpikinin is olive oil, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:3:2.english: And pampers the skin - [In Old French:] esclairer [to brighten or clear].

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:4:1.hebrew: שיהא בקי בהן - שידע ממה הן עושין אותו, שיהא נזהר בהן. כשיביאו לו כותח, ידע שיש חלב ויש שם חמץ, אם פסח הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:4:1.english: That he will be well-versed in them - So that he will know from what they make it, [and] that he should be careful with them. When they bring him kutach, he will know that there is milk [in it] and that there is chametz there, if it is Passover.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:5:1.english: Matkilta - Some relish with which to eat the bread.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:5:2.english: Once he heard - that they called its name kutach.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:5:3.english: He withdrew - For he was knowledgeable and knew that there is milk in it.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:7:1.hebrew: מאן תנא - דמתני' דאית ליה חמץ דגן גמור שנתערב במין אחר ואינו בעין שנימוח, אי נמי חמץ נוקשה רע ואיתיה בעיניה, מוזהרין על אכילתו בלאו? דקתני מתניתין: כותח הבבלי ושכר המדי — חמץ דגן גמור, אלא שנתערב בדבר אחר; ותכשיטי נשים — בעיניה הוא, אבל נוקשה הוא, דאינו ראוי לאכילה; וקתני באזהרה, דעובר עליהן בלאו:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:7:1.english: Who is the Tanna - [i.e.,] of our Mishnah, who holds [that] leaven of full-fledged grain that was mixed with another kind [of food] and is not intact, as it has dissolved, or else inferior hardened leaven that is intact — one is warned against eating it with a negative commandment? For our Mishnah teaches: Babylonian kutach and Median beer [are] leaven of full-fledged grain, except that it was mixed with something else; and women's cosmetics — [their leaven] is intact, but it is hardened, as it is not fit for eating; and [the Mishnah] teaches [them] as a prohibition, that one transgresses a negative commandment through them.

Rashi on Pesachim 43a:8:1.hebrew: שיאור - שלא נתחמץ כל צורכו. שיאור פליגי במתני': ר"מ קרי שיאור את שהכסיפו פניו, וזהו תחלת חימוצו, ולר' יהודה הוי שיאור שהתחיל ליסדק כבר סדקין דקין כקרני חגבים, אחד לכאן ואחד לכאן; אבל שהכסיפו פניו — לרבי יהודה מצה היא, ולר"מ קרני חגבים חמץ גמור הוא. והכא הכי קאמר: שיאור ישרף — דאסור בהנאה: שיאור דר"מ, הכסיפו פניו, ישרף לר"מ, ושיאור דרבי יהודה ישרף לר' יהודה. וסיפא דקתני ונותנו לפני כלבו — אליבא דרבי יהודה קאמר ליה, ואשיאור דר"מ קאי. והאוכלו בארבעים — אתאן לר"מ, כלומר: לר"מ, האוכלו לשיאור זה, שרבי יהודה מתיר בהנאה, סופג את הארבעים. אלמא שמעינן ליה לר"מ דאית ליה חדא מהני תרתי דמתני', דקאמר נוקשה בעיני' בלאו — כגון שיאור, דנוקשה הוא, דאינו ראוי לאכילה הואיל והחמיץ קצת ולא גמר, ולהחמיץ עיסות אחרות כשאור נמי לא חזי — וקאמר בלאו, וכ"ש חמץ גמור ע"י תערובת, דקסבר רב יהודה ע"י תערובת חמיר מנוקשה בעין. והאי לאו דנוקשה נפקא ליה מכל מחמצת לא תאכלו — כל רבויא הוא, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 43a:8:1.english: Si'ur [partially leavened dough] - [Dough] that has not leavened completely. [Regarding] si'ur, they disagree in the Mishnah: Rabbi Meir calls si'ur that whose surface has paled, and this is the beginning of its leavening; whereas according to Rabbi Yehuda, si'ur is that which has already begun to crack with fine cracks like the antennae of locusts, one this way and one that way. However, that whose surface has paled is [still] matzah according to Rabbi Yehuda, and [dough with] locust-antennae [cracks] is full-fledged chametz according to Rabbi Meir. And here [the baraita] is saying as follows: "Si'ur must be burned" — for it is forbidden [to derive] benefit [from it]: the si'ur of Rabbi Meir, [whose] surface has paled, must be burned according to Rabbi Meir, and the si'ur of Rabbi Yehuda must be burned according to Rabbi Yehuda. And the latter clause that teaches "and he places it before his dog" — it states this according to Rabbi Yehuda, and it refers to the si'ur of Rabbi Meir. "And one who eats it [is flogged] with forty [lashes]" — we have arrived at [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir; that is to say, according to Rabbi Meir, one who eats this si'ur — from which Rabbi Yehuda permits [deriving] benefit — incurs the forty [lashes]. Thus we learn about Rabbi Meir that he holds one of these two [cases] of our Mishnah, for he says [that] nuksheh [inferior leaven] in its pure state [is punishable] by a negative commandment — such as si'ur, which is nuksheh, since it is not fit for eating because it has leavened slightly and has not finished, and it is also not fit to leaven other doughs as sourdough — and he says [it is punishable] by a negative commandment, and all the more so full-fledged chametz through a mixture, since Rav Yehuda holds [that chametz] through a mixture is more severe than nuksheh in its pure state. And this negative commandment for nuksheh he derives from "you shall not eat anything leavened" — "anything" [kol] is an inclusion, as [will be explained] below.

Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:10:1.hebrew: ונותנו לפני כלבו דר"מ לרבי יהודה - מדאורייתא אפי' באכילה שרי, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דחולין (דף כג:) דמצה מעלייתא היא; אלא מדרבנן אסור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:10:1.english: "And one gives it to his dog — [leavening] of Rabbi Meir according to Rabbi Yehuda" - By Torah law it is even permitted to be eaten, as we say in the first chapter of Chullin (23b) that it is proper matzah; rather, by rabbinic law it is prohibited.

Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:19:1.hebrew: ואילו נוקשה בעיניה לא קתני - וא"ת: ונימא דמשום הכי לא חשיב ליה, משום דכ"ש הוא, כדאמר רב נחמן? וי"ל: דאי כ"ש הוא, הוה ליה למיתני, לאשמועינן דלית ביה כרת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:19:1.english: Yet hardened [leaven] in its pure form it does not teach - And if you ask: Let us say that for this reason [the baraita] did not list it, because it is all the more so, as Rav Nachman said? One can answer: If it were all the more so, it should have taught [it] to teach us that there is no karet for it:

Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:25:1.hebrew: ההוא כל לאתויי נשים - תימה לר"י: הא תרי "כי כל" כתיבי גבי כרת — "כי כל אוכל חמץ ונכרתה" ו"כי כל אוכל מחמצת", ונרבינן עירובו לכרת! ואפילו לרבנן דלא דרשי "כל", "כי כל" דרשי. ואור"י דפשיטא ליה לגמרא דאתא לשום דרשא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:25:1.english: That [term] kol [is needed] to include women - This is surprising to the Ri: Behold, two [instances of] "for whosoever [ki khol]" are written regarding karet — "for whosoever eats leavened bread, [that soul] shall be cut off" and "for whosoever eats anything leavened" — and [thus] we should include its mixture for karet! And even according to the Rabbis, who do not expound "kol," they do expound "ki khol"! And the Ri says that it is obvious to the Gemara that it comes for some [other] exposition:

Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:4:1.hebrew: למה מנו חכמים את אלו - תימה לרשב"א: הא איצטריך למנותם לאשמועינן שהן בלאו ולא בכרת! ותירץ ר"י, דלא הוה ליה לאשמועינן אלא תרי מינייהו: חד לנוקשה בעיניה, וחד ע"י תערובת. ועוד הקשה, דת"ק שמנאם לית ליה האי כללא, דהא איכא תכשיטי נשים שהן מין דגן ואין עובר בפסח, אלא רבי אליעזר הוא דקאמר לה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:4:1.english: Why did the Sages list these? - This is puzzling to Rashba: surely it was necessary to list them to teach us that they are [subject to] a negative prohibition and not karet! And Ri answered that [the Tanna] only needed to teach us two of them: one for hardened [leaven] on its own, and one [prohibited] through a mixture. And [Rashba] further asked: the first Tanna (Tanna Kamma) who listed them does not hold of this general principle, since there are women's cosmetics that are a type of grain and yet one does not transgress [the prohibition] on Passover [with them]; rather, it is Rabbi Eliezer who states it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:7:1.hebrew: מאן תנא חמץ גמור ע"י תערובת ונוקשה בעיניה בלאו - משמע בשמעתין דאי לאו דאיתרבי חמץ נוקשה למלקות, אפילו איסור לא היה בו. ותימה לר"י, דבפ"ק דחולין (דף כג:) בעי רבי זירא: "הרי עלי לחמי תודה מן החמץ או מן המצה" והביא שיאור, מהו? שיאור דמאן? אי דר"מ, לר"מ מדלקי עליה חמץ הוא! והשתא מנא ליה דהוי חמץ לענין תודה? דילמא שאני חמץ בפסח דרבייה קרא למלקות (גרידא)! ואור"י דהתם נמי איכא שום קרא דמרבינן מיניה חמץ נוקשה. והא דתניא בפרק כל המנחות באות מצה (מנחות דף נג:): "אין מחמיצין בתפוחים" — דהוי חמץ נוקשה כדמשמע התם — היינו לכתחילה, אבל בדיעבד כשר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 43a:7:1.english: Who is the tanna [who holds that] full-fledged leaven through a mixture and hardened [leaven] in its pure form are subject to a negative prohibition - It is implied in our sugya that were it not for [the fact] that hardened leaven was included [by a verse] for lashes, there would not even be a prohibition in it. And this is astonishing to the Ri, for in the first chapter of Chullin (23b), Rabbi Zeira asks: [If one says,] "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] the loaves of a thanksgiving offering from the leavened or from the unleavened," and he brought si'ur [partially leavened dough], what is [the law]? [The Gemara there asks:] Si'ur according to whom? If according to Rabbi Meir — according to Rabbi Meir, since one incurs lashes for it, it is [considered] leaven! Now, from where does he know that it is [considered] leaven regarding a thanksgiving offering? Perhaps leaven on Passover is different, since the verse included it for lashes (alone)! And the Ri says that there too [regarding the thanksgiving offering], there is some verse from which we include hardened leaven. And that which was taught in the chapter Kol HaMenachot Ba'ot Matzah (Menachot 53b): "One may not leaven [the loaves] with apples" — which is hardened leaven, as is implied there — that is ab initio, but ex post facto it is valid:
